subject: Recap + next tests: competitive qualification and hallucination rundown
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@edgeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next tests: competitive qualification and hallucination rundown

Emily — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a concrete set of next tests so we can move from conversation -> apples-to-apples evaluation. High level notes:

- Your priorities: reduce hallucination in customer-facing replies, predictable p95 latency under 500ms for typical short queries, and meaningful unit-cost savings versus your current HyperscalerX contract.
- Current baseline: HyperscalerX text-inference (v2026.6), mixed prompt lengths (6–120 tokens), two-shot system prompts for some flows.
- Constraints: no PII leave, prefer minimal data egress, and engineering wants a reproducible test harness.

Agreed next tests (owners & timeline):
1) Quality suite (owner: Marcus) — 1k prompt regression set focusing on factual QA, instruction-following, and safety probes. Metrics: hallucination_rate, EM (exact match) for fact items, and human-rated coherence on a 1–5 scale. Target initial results by 2026-12-15.
2) Performance run (owner: Ben) — P95/P99 latency and throughput (1–100 concurrent qps) across: Redwood hosted model variants, Redwood quantized profile, and HyperscalerX baseline. Include token-cost calculation per response.
3) Adversarial/hallucination probes (owner: Marcus) — a focused set (~150 prompts) that historically trigger hallucinations (time-sensitive facts, ambiguous context).
4) Regression guardrail plan (owner: Jordan) — snapshot baseline + daily rerun for first 2 weeks, then weekly. Alert if hallucination_rate increases by >3 percentage points or p95 latency degrades by >20%.

Action items for EdgeAI: share the small sample S3 bucket with the 1k prompt set or confirm a sanitized subset we can use. For our side: we will provide a test matrix and a runbook to reproduce runs in a controlled environment (attached: edgeai-test-matrix.xlsx).

Next calendar step: one-hour deep-dive next Wed to review the prompt suite and the HyperscalerX side-by-side. Please confirm a time window that works for your team.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

[attachment: edgeai-test-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@edgeai.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Dec 2026 08:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next tests: competitive qualification and hallucination rundown

Quick coordination notes and a proposed test plan we can hand to EdgeAI during the deep-dive:

Plan overview (step-by-step):
- Environment: Redwood hosted sandbox (isolated tenant), Redwood quantized profile, HyperscalerX API (customer-provided credentials).
- Canonicalization: normalize prompts (strip user metadata), fix random_seed where applicable, run with deterministic sampling for quality comparisons and with temperature=0.2 and temperature=0.8 for variance checks.
- Metrics to compute per prompt:
  * hallucination_rate (binary — answer contains unverifiable fact compared to ground truth)
  * exact_match (where ground truth exists)
  * answer_length_tokens (avg)
  * cost_per_response_usd (based on token counts & each provider's price table)
  * latency_ms_p95/p99

Eval prompt categories (examples): fact-check QA, multi-hop inference, temporal queries (time-sensitive), instruction following (summarize/transform), long-context retrieval tests, safety/adversarial probes.

Regression guardrails: store baseline hashes and log-prob distributions; daily rerun for production mirror tests; auto-flag if hallucination_rate delta > 3pp or p95 latency regresses > 20% from baseline.

I'll attach a short runbook and a helper script we use to pull token counts and compute cost estimates — attaching runbook-quickstart.md. Marcus, can you confirm which quantization profiles we should include for an apples-to-apples latency vs cost sweep?

— Ben
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: runbook-quickstart.md (markdown)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@edgeai.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Dec 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next tests: competitive qualification and hallucination rundown

Thanks — adding technical specifics and a proposed prompt fixture set. High level approach: run each provider across three axes (quality, cost, latency) and report both aggregate metrics and per-prompt deltas so we can spot regressions tied to prompt classes.

Prompt fixtures (short names):
- knowledge_check: short factual queries with ground truth (EM candidate).
- temporal_facts: queries with a time horizon ("Who is the CEO of X in 2018?").
- doc_lookup: provide a short doc and ask for citation-aware answers.
- instruction_transform: long -> concise; paraphrase; format convert.
- adversarial_nudge: ambiguous prompts designed to trigger confabulation.
- long_context: 1–8k token contexts to test KV cache behavior.

Hallucination measurement approach:
1) automated match against curated ground truth where available (EM/F1).
2) blind human verification for free-form answers (human raters mark ungrounded claims).
3) source-attribution check for doc_lookup tasks (does the model cite the provided doc?).

Quantization & runtime notes:
- We'll run: fp16 baseline, q4_0 and q5_0 profiles. Expect roughly 20–30% latency improvement with q4_0 at modest quality trade-offs; q5_0 is more aggressive. We'll include both so EdgeAI can see latency vs generated quality carefully.
- For long_context tests, run with KV caching enabled and disabled to measure cold-start vs warm-run behavior.

Attachments: prompt-suite-v1.json (the initial prompt fixtures), model-comparison-summary.md (how we'll format the side-by-side). I'll also export a small script that computes token counts + cost_estimates; Ben has the runbook.

Planned deliverable: a one-sheet comparing Redwood variants vs HyperscalerX with the following columns: prompt_id, prompt_class, EM, hallucination_flag, avg_tokens, cost_usd, p95_latency_ms, provider_notes.

Marcus
Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
